title: FSS flags 28 AI-driven hacking IPs, orders South Korea finance to shore up defenses
key_facts: On 6 Oct 2026 the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), South Korea's financial regulator, said in a notice that it circulated 33 IP addresses that attempted hacking tied to recent security incidents in the financial sector, or 28 after removing duplicates, with some country information.
The hacking attacks are presumed to have used AI agents.
The FSS had shared 19 attacker IPs with the industry the previous day; as of that day the IPs spanned 12 countries, with the United States most common at five, plus one domestic IP.

Hackers of unknown nationality tunnelled through IPs in various countries, explored multiple services in financial firms' systems, found vulnerabilities and launched concentrated attacks; the FSS warns that some IPs cannot be tied to a country and that caution is needed in interpreting country data.

The FSS narrowed the list using IPs that accessed through abnormal routes and stole customers' personal information from some banks, including Shinhan Bank, and asked institutions to complete self-inspections and fixes by 8 Oct.

It also sent a 12-item checklist asking, among other things, whether the shared attacker IPs are blocked, whether there were intrusion attempts or damage tied to them, and whether real-time security monitoring is running.
Toss Bank, an internet-only bank, found abnormal access attempts through flagged IPs in July and August and as early as January.

Some in the cybersecurity industry suspect a China-origin attack because of traces of a Chinese-language AI penetration testing tool disclosed in July, but authorities have not named any country of origin.
quote_evidence: Financial authorities identified 28 internet protocol (IP) addresses in connection with hacking attacks on the financial sector that are presumed to have used artificial intelligence (AI) agents.

However, the FSS emphasized in the notice that "some IPs cannot be tied to a specific country, and even if a country is identified, there is a possibility of circumvention, so caution is needed in interpretation."

In the case of Toss Bank, an internet-only bank, it found that not only in July–August this year but also as early as January there were abnormal access attempts via some attacker IPs flagged by authorities.
why_it_matters_hint: A regulator has put a concrete list of attacker addresses and a deadline in front of the whole financial sector, though AI use and the attackers' location are still unproven.
event_date: FSS notice 6 Oct 2026; the attacks were first reported 2 to 3 Oct 2026
notes: Read in full. Follow-up of our 5 Oct 2026 item on seven financial companies hit by hacks (pool 1005:C12-02). The article lists Japan twice in its country list. Yonhap carried the same 28-address news on 6 Oct. Same story line as C12-01 and C12-14; C12-14 quotes a Financial Security Institute official saying AI was used as a tool by a human hacker, which this article does not.
